result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: Under § 473(b), the court may, on just terms, relieve a party from a judgment, dismissal, order or other proceeding taken against the party.
claims.quote: (b) The court may, upon any terms as may be just, relieve a party or the party’s legal representative from a judgment, dismissal, order, or other proceeding taken against the party

claims.claim: The grounds are the party’s mistake, inadvertence, surprise or excusable neglect that caused the adverse result.
claims.quote: taken against the party through the party’s mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect.

claims.claim: The request for this relief must include a copy of the proposed answer or other pleading.
claims.quote: Application for this relief shall be accompanied by a copy of the answer or other pleading proposed to be filed therein, otherwise the application shall not be granted

claims.claim: The request must be made within a reasonable time.
claims.quote: and shall be made within a reasonable time, in no case exceeding six months
claims.note: Six months is an outer limit, not a guarantee that waiting that long is reasonable.

claims.claim: The request may not be made more than six months after the judgment, dismissal, order or proceeding was taken.
claims.quote: in no case exceeding six months, after the judgment, dismissal, order, or proceeding was taken.
claims.note: This deadline concerns the discretionary relief described in subdivision (b).

claims.claim: Under § 473(a)(1), the court has discretion, after notice to the other side, to allow an answer after the code’s time limit.
claims.quote: The court may likewise, in its discretion, after notice to the adverse party, allow, upon any terms as may be just, an amendment to any pleading or proceeding in other particulars; and may upon like terms allow an answer to be made after the time limited by this code.
claims.note: The court may impose just terms.

claims.claim: Under § 473(d), either party may move, after notice to the other, for the court to set aside any void judgment or order.
claims.quote: and may, on motion of either party after notice to the other party, set aside any void judgment or order.

claims.claim: The current version remains in effect through December 31, 2026.
claims.quote: (e) This section shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2027, and as of that date is repealed.

claims.claim: The replacement version becomes operative January 1, 2027.
claims.quote: (f) This section shall become operative on January 1, 2027.

claims.claim: The replacement retains the wording of subdivisions (a) through (d).
The new subdivision (e) replaces the repeal provision.
claims.quote: The old subdivision (e) (repeal on January 1, 2027) is replaced by a new (e) on motions to vacate a default judgment void for lack of proper service

claims.claim: Under the new subdivision (e), a party may move at any time after entry to vacate a default judgment void for lack of proper service.
claims.quote: (e) Notwithstanding any other requirements of this section, a party to an action may bring a motion to vacate a default judgment that is void for lack of proper service at any time after entry of the judgment.
claims.note: The provision addresses when the motion may be brought; it does not guarantee relief.

flags.text: Starting January 1, 2027, subdivision (e) expressly permits a motion at any time after entry for a default judgment void for lack of proper service. The draft distinguishes this future rule from current law.

result.summary: All draft claims are supported within the stated scope. The draft distinguishes the reasonable-time requirement from the six-month ceiling for discretionary relief under § 473(b).
